svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Except as in Article 9.20.1.2., this Section
applies to walls not in contact with the
ground
(a) unreinforced masonry and masonry veneer
walls, where (i) the walls built on the
foundation walls are not more than 11 m (36′-1⅛″)
high and (ii) the roof or floor assembly above
the first storey is not of concrete construction,
and (b) flat insulating concrete form walls that
(i) have a maximum floor-to-floor height of 3 m
(9′-10⅛″), (ii) are in buildings not more than 2
storeys in building height, and (iii) are in
locations where Smax for Site Class C is not
greater than 0.27 (see also Article 9.4.2.5.).
For other walls, or masonry or ICF walls
designed for specified loads on the basis of
ultimate and serviceability limit states,
Subsection 4.3.2. applies.
Flat ICF walls
ICF walls are concrete walls cast into
manufactured insulating forms that stay in place
after the concrete has cured. Flat ICF walls are
solid, with concrete of uniform thickness over
the height and width of the wall.
Drawn: walls cut through, floors cut back, roofs not shown. Storey heights in A are illustration only.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.20.1.1. (page 9-137)
